cr_data.provenance:
1929-1986: Collection of the artist, Abiquiu, New Mexico 
1986-1994: The Georgia O’Keeffe Foundation, Santa Fe, New Mexico 
1994-Present: Dallas Museum of Art, gift from above 
(Source: Dallas Museum of Art, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Sold to Sir Joseph Duveen. Note: O'Keeffe says this is a katchina." O'Keeffe, and subsequently Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks, confused this painting with work Duveen purchased in 1932, see cat. no. 781. Backing inscription dates 1924? Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks date 1929. Dated 1929 on basis of inclusion in 1930 New York (An American Place) exhibition; pictured in Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 36. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Layered circles in shades of green, pale blue, and pale pink, spiral inward from the edges of the abstract composition towards its middle. In the center of these circles are several narrow forms with rounded tops that resemble stamens in the center of a flower. These forms are painted in shades of dark blue, pale blue, and gray.
